modelBlurb: Rank each of the ten stats within Division I, drop each program’s single best and single worst percentile, average the other eight.

provenance.perception: Weeks in the AP poll and weeks in the AP top 10, every poll since 1949-50, preseason and final polls included. Through 2015-16 from Sports-Reference’s poll archive; since then from the AP rank ESPN carries on each game (data/basketball/staging/_staging_ap_poll_success.csv).
provenance.wins: Division I wins and losses season by season (Sports-Reference through 2015-16, ESPN game results since). NCAA-vacated wins are removed in the NCAA official view (data/basketball/staging/_staging_wins.csv).
provenance.championships: NCAA tournament titles since 1939, and conference regular-season titles (co-champions count in full) — computed from conference games since 1950, earlier titles from Sports-Reference’s all-time totals. A title the NCAA vacated (Louisville 2013) counts only in the as-played view (data/basketball/staging/_staging_championships.csv, _staging_conference_titles.csv).
provenance.allAmericans: Consensus first-team All-Americans since 1949-50, and national players of the year (UPI 1955–60, AP 1961–68, Naismith since 1969). Compiled by hand and still being verified against the NCAA record book (data/basketball/staging/_staging_all_americans.csv, _staging_player_of_year.csv).
provenance.nflDraft: Every NCAA tournament since 1939: Sweet 16s (reached the regional semifinals; every team in the 8- and 16-team fields of 1939–52) and Final Fours. Vacated runs count only in the as-played view (data/basketball/staging/_staging_ncaa_tournament.csv).

tierDescriptions.Blue Bloods: The programs the data sets clearly apart at the top. Each has hung banners across multiple eras, on sustained excellence rather than one run.
tierDescriptions.Blue Blood Fringe: Just outside the inner circle. Their histories carry too much weight to ignore, and the numbers place them firmly in the tier right below the top.
tierDescriptions.Blue Blood Contenders: The next tier, where the path to the top is less defined. Each has the history and the March résumé to make a run at blue-blood status, but needs more decades of sustained success — or a truly dominant era — to close the gap.
tierDescriptions.National Powers: Programs the whole country knows, with real Final Four history. The band runs from genuine current risers to powers coasting on an era two or three decades back.
tierDescriptions.National Brands: Recognisable names and real tournament pedigrees, but a clear class break below the powers. Also where newer high-major programs still accruing the cumulative totals land.
tierDescriptions.The Field: Everyone else — mostly one-bid leagues, regional followings and thin résumés, plus the young Division I programs whose ceilings haven’t been tested by the counting stats.

granular.allAmericans: per-player list for 97/365 programs; the rest (no consensus selections) sit at zero.
granular.conferenceTitles: per-year for 331/365 programs (_staging_conference_titles.csv); the rest use a summary total

dataRange: AP poll 1949-50 → 2025-26; Division I records from the 1890s; NCAA tournament from 1939; All-Americans from 1949-50 — our own compilation
